newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Shares in Unicer suspended in Lisbon.
newsitem.headline: Shares in Unicer suspended in Lisbon.

text.p: Trade in shares in drinks group Unicer was halted on Tuesday by the Lisbon bourse authorities, dealers said.
They said that the suspension apparently followed news reports that the drinks group was preparing a counter-offer for mineral water company Vidago

The Diario Economico newspaper reported that Unicer was interested in bidding for Vidago after retailer Jeronimo Martins said it would launch a bid, valuing Portugal's leading sparkling water supplier at 15.8 billion escudos.

The paper quoted a source close to Unicer, which distributes beer, mineral water, wine and juices, as saying his company was interested in acquiring Vidago, even though it believed the price bid by Jeronimo Martins was too high.
Jeronimo Martins said on Saturday it would launch a bid for Vidago at around 4,270 escudos per share.
If Unicer offered to buy Vidago, it would have to offer a price that was at least five percent higher than the previous bid, according to Portuguese law.
A Unicer spokesman, contacted by Reuters, declined comment on the company's reported interest in Vidago.
The Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) today ended a suspension in trade in Vidago shares on Lisbon bourse.
